storage.title: Storage
storage.what_is_what: The database, the original uploads and the catalog are protected and are never deleted from here. Intermediates are produced automatically by import and cleaning; exports are copies that can be generated again.
storage.retention_hint: Exports older than this are removed when the server starts. “Off” means nothing is ever deleted on its own.
storage.opt_intermediates_hint: normalized.csv is read once during import, and cleaned.csv is written only to measure its own size. Neither is read again, and both are rebuilt when needed.
storage.opt_all_exports_hint: Not just the expired ones. Exports are copies of data still held in the database and can be exported again.

backup.title: Backups
backup.no_backup_warning: There is no backup. The data exists on one disk only.
backup.same_disk_warning: Backups are on the same disk as the data. That survives a bad cleaning run or a deleted file, but not the disk failing - point BACKUP_DIR at another drive.
backup.how_it_works: Each database is snapshotted through DuckDB rather than copied as a file - copying a live file captures a half-written page and produces a corrupt one. Every written file is then reopened, its rows counted, and compared against the counts taken while snapshotting; nothing is called verified unless the two agree.
backup.opt_originals_hint: Much larger. Worth adding if you no longer keep the source file anywhere else.
backup.schedule_hint: Checked every half hour: if the newest verified backup is older than the chosen interval, one is taken. A machine that was switched off does not miss its window - it backs up as soon as it returns.
backup.stale_never: No backup has ever been taken

lockouts.title: Temporarily locked
lockouts.hint: After repeated failed logins, attempts are held off for a while, and the wait doubles with each further failure. The lock is always temporary - a permanent one would let anyone who knows a username take that person's access away. Every active lock is listed here and can be lifted by hand.
lockouts.subject: Name / address

compaction.title: Compact databases
compaction.hint: A database file does not shrink on its own: imports and cleaning runs leave empty pages behind inside it. Compaction rewrites the file with only what it actually holds - verifying the new copy row by row before replacing the old one, and leaving the original untouched if that verification fails.
compaction.already_compact: The file is already compact; it was left untouched.

activity_trim.title: Trim the activity log
activity_trim.hint: This never runs on its own: not one line goes without you picking a period, pressing the button and confirming. The log is append-only, and it is trimmed by age alone — not by entry and not by user, because the first line worth erasing is the one somebody wants gone. The trim itself is recorded.

housekeeping.title: Operation history
housekeeping.hint: This runs on its own - every half hour, and at every start. Unlike export retention and the activity log it needs no switching on, because what it removes is neither a file somebody asked for nor evidence: it is a row saying an operation finished months ago.
housekeeping.jobs_hint: One row per import, quality check, export, backup and compaction. A job that has not finished is never removed however old it looks - age is not evidence it is over.
housekeeping.held: And {{count}} export rows kept past their date: the file is still downloadable, and the row is what tells the download endpoint its format.
housekeeping.cleaning_hint: A longer period, deliberately: this is the record of what was done to the data - how many rows a run removed, which columns it dropped - not a note that something ran.
